slides.headline: Florida’s dengue outbreak is the largest in decades
slides.body: Florida now has the largest dengue outbreak in the continental U.S. in decades. The concern is local mosquito-borne spread as cases keep rising.

slides.headline: Florida dengue cases hit a record 252
slides.body: Florida reached 252 reported dengue cases on Oct. 2. The case count is still climbing.

slides.headline: Locally acquired cases rose to 252
slides.body: Florida had 252 locally acquired dengue cases on Oct. 2. Local transmission means people caught the virus in Florida.

slides.headline: Over 250 cases were reported by Oct. 2
slides.body: CBS News reported more than 250 cases on Oct. 2. WUSF said the outbreak is the largest in the continental U.S. in decades.

slides.headline: Underreporting is now part of the concern
slides.body: ABC News reported concerns about underreporting as dengue keeps rising in Florida. Dengue infections can be mild or have no symptoms.
